title: Interviewer Workload Equality and Candidate Experience Playbook
author: Maya Chen
content:
Summary:

This playbook defines Redwood's interviewer workload equality policy and the candidate-facing SLAs that preserve a high-quality, predictable interview experience. It provides concrete rules, a lightweight algorithm for balancing interviewer assignments across teams, scheduling and debrief SLOs, escalation paths for capacity shortages, and an operational runbook for people-ops and hiring managers.

Purpose
- Ensure interview load is equitably distributed across qualified interviewers to reduce burnout and bias introduced by uneven paneling.
- Guarantee a consistent candidate experience by defining measurable SLAs for scheduling, communication, and decision cadence.
- Provide a repeatable operational procedure for people-ops and hiring managers to handle surges, special-case roles, and urgent hiring needs.

Scope
- Applies to all technical and non-technical interview panels coordinated by Redwood hiring teams (full-time, contractor > 3 months, internships).
- Does NOT modify role-specific assessment rubrics (those remain in hiring scorecard docs).
- Includes exceptions for executive-level hiring; see Exceptions section.

Key Principles
1. Bias minimization: distribute interview volume so no single interviewer systematically influences multiple decisions for the same role or candidate cohort.
2. Transparency: candidates receive clear scheduling windows and decision timelines.
3. Fair load: aim for predictable weekly interview quotas per interviewer with opt-outs recorded and respected.
4. Escalation: clear escalation channels when capacity or scheduling SLAs cannot be met.

Definitions
- Interview Unit: one 45–60 minute candidate interview slot (including buffer).
- Interview Bandwidth: number of Interview Units an interviewer is scheduled for in a given week.
- Panel Owner: hiring manager who owns debriefs and final recommendation for a role.

SLAs (Candidate-facing)
- Initial scheduling window: candidate should be offered at least two time options within 48 hours of phone-screen pass.
- Schedule confirmation: interview invites must be sent with calendar links and prep notes at least 72 hours before the slot.
- Decision cadence: first pass decision (advance/reject) communicated to candidate within 5 business days after final on-site/debrief.
- Offer timeline (target): verbal offer within 2 business days after Panel Owner sign-off; written offer within 3 business days.

Interviewer Load Targets and Thresholds
- Healthy target: 3–4 Interview Units/week for active interviewers.
- Upper soft limit: 6 Interview Units/week. When an interviewer reaches 6, automatic reassignment notifications trigger.
- Opt-in minimum: interviewer must have completed interviewer calibration and be listed as active in the Interviewer Roster to receive assignments.
- Cooling period: after leading 2 hiring decisions (Panel Owner role) in a 30-day window, recommend 1 week lighter load.

Balancing Algorithm (lightweight, deterministic)
1. Maintain an Interviewer Roster with attributes: team, role domain, calibrated_level (junior|mid|senior), weekly_capacity (integer), last_week_units (integer).
2. For each open interview slot, assign the lowest-last-week_units interviewer who: matches role domain, is calibrated, and has weekly_capacity > 0.
3. If multiple candidates tie, prefer same-team interviewers up to 40% of panel to preserve domain knowledge; remaining panelists must be cross-functional.
4. If no calibrated interviewer available in domain, fallback to cross-functional senior interviewer and flag people-ops.

Operational Rules and Process (step-by-step)
1. Requisition opens: Hiring manager fills Hiring Intake form and selects desired domains and preferred interviewers. People-ops ingests the form and creates a Panel Plan in Greenhouse/ATS.
2. People-ops runs automated assignment job (daily) to populate interview slots for the next 14 calendar days according to the balancing algorithm.
3. Notification: assigned interviewers receive an email + Slack DM with candidate context and prep notes 96 hours before the interview. If the slot is within 72 hours at assignment time, interviewer must ack within 6 hours or an auto-reassign will occur.
4. Candidate scheduling: Scheduler (people-ops or hiring coordinator) presents candidate with two options within 48 hours.
5. Debrief: Panel Owner opens debrief within 24 hours of interview completion. Interviewers must complete written feedback within 24 hours.
6. Decision: Panel Owner gathers feedback, makes decision, and communicates to people-ops within 48 hours of last feedback. People-ops then triggers candidate outreach per SLA.

Escalation and Capacity Shortage Play
- When daily assignment job fails to find a calibrated interviewer for > 10% of slots for a role bucket, people-ops triggers "Capacity Alert" to the Recruitment Operations lead and the Hiring Managers of impacted roles.
- If scheduling/SLA breaches exceed 12 hours for > 3 candidates in a rolling 7-day window: open an incident with Priority-Medium; people-ops coordinates short-term temp interviewer contributions from adjacent teams.
- For urgent hiring (business-critical or revenue-impacting roles), hiring manager can request a temporary pool by filing a Rapid Support Request; people-ops has 48 hours to staff a 2-person interim panel.

Exception Handling
- Executive hires: by default outside algorithm; hiring manager and Head of People coordinate bespoke panels.
- International timezones: when candidate's timezone prevents meeting SLA windows, use asynchronous take-home assessments + on-demand interviewer scheduling; still require decision cadence parity.

Reporting and Metrics
- Weekly dashboards (owned by people-ops):
  - Average Interview Units/week per interviewer (target mean 3.5, stdev < 1.8)
  - % of panels with at least one cross-functional interviewer = target >= 60%
  - Scheduling SLA compliance: % scheduled within 48 hours (target 90%)
  - Debrief compliance: % of interview feedback submitted within 24 hours (target 95%)
  - SLA breach incidents and root cause notes

Runbook: Immediate actions for SLA breach (for people-ops oncall)
1. Identify affected candidates and roles via dashboard filter.
2. Notify Hiring Manager and propose two immediate fixes: a) reassign available calibrated interviewers; b) convert to shorter paired interviews (two 30-miners) with increased prep notes.
3. If candidate communication delayed > 48 hours, send templated apology + new timeline and offer priority scheduling.
4. Log incident in status board, perform 7-day follow-up retrospective and add corrective actions to monthly hiring ops review.

Training and Calibration
- Interviewer certification: mandatory 2-hour calibration session every 6 months (materials in /confluence/people-ops/interview-calibration-and-hiring-scorecard-guidelines-2025).
- New interviewer shadowing: 3 shadowed interviews and 2 co-interviews before being eligible for independent scheduling.

Ownership and Review Cadence
- People-ops: owns roster maintenance, automated assignment job, SLA dashboards, and incident runbook.
- Hiring Managers: own panel composition, final decisions, and should flag exceptional time commitments in hiring intake.
- Monthly review: people-ops and recruitment ops review metrics and publish a short "health note" to hiring managers.

Appendix: Sample scheduling table (example constraints)
| Constraint | Value | Action if violated |
|---|---:|---|
| Candidate scheduling window | 48 hours | Escalate to hiring coordinator |
| Interview prep delivery | 72 hours before slot | Notify interviewer and auto-reassign if <6-hour ack |
| Interviewer weekly soft cap | 6 units | Auto-notify interviewer and stop new non-critical assignments |

FAQ (short)
Q: Can engineers opt out of interviews temporarily?
A: Yes — record opt-outs in the roster; people-ops will respect the opt-out for the stated duration.

Q: What happens if an interviewer consistently misses debriefs?
A: People-ops flags repeated misses (3 in 30 days) to their manager for a coaching conversation; repeated patterns escalate to HR review.
